headline: Houston's sound is slowed down on purpose: slab, screw and trunk-rattling bass are a Black Southside tradition the Rockets can wear, if Nike credits the neighborhoods that built it.
summary: Houston music runs on tempo and pride: DJ Screw's chopped-and-screwed tapes out of the Third Ward and South Park, Rap-A-Lot and the Geto Boys from the Fifth Ward, Swishahouse's mid-2000s boom, and a current wave led by Travis Scott, Megan Thee Stallion, Don Toliver and Alief's Maxo Kream and Tobe Nwigwe. Under hip-hop sits older Houston: Duke-Peacock blues and Lightnin' Hopkins, zydeco from Frenchtown, Tejano and a huge immigrant music scene in the southwest. The sound has a physical culture attached (slabs with candy paint and swangas, grills, wood-grain, trunk art) that is the richest design vocabulary in the market. The Rockets' 2026-27 ketchup-and-mustard throwback look and a Durant-Sengun-Thompson team give a natural bridge, but the scene respects those who pay it back locally.

insights.title: Slow is the signature
insights.detail: Chopped and screwed, pioneered by DJ Screw and the Screwed Up Click from the Southside in the 1990s, slows tempo and stretches pitch so music feels heavy and syrupy. It is Houston's single most identifiable export and a mood, not just a genre.
insights.implication: Tell the Rockets story through slowed-down, heavy, unhurried design (long gradients, stretched type, blur and smear graphics) rather than speed and aggression.

insights.title: The car is the stage
insights.detail: Slab culture (candy-painted older Cadillacs and Chevys with swangas or elbows, big chrome wheels, trunk displays) is how Black Houston shows its music and status, from Third Ward Sunday cruising to the Art Car Parade crossover.
insights.implication: Candy paint, chrome and trunk-display graphics are authentic materials and finishes for footwear, jerseys and outerwear; partner with slab builders and clubs instead of imitating them.

insights.title: Two ends of the city, two sounds
insights.detail: The Fifth Ward gave the Geto Boys and Rap-A-Lot (and Duke-Peacock Records before them); the Third Ward and South Park gave Screw, Lil' Keke, Trae tha Truth and Beyonce. Southwest Alief is now the engine for Maxo Kream and Tobe Nwigwe, with a Vietnamese, Nigerian and Latino mix.
insights.implication: Build neighborhood-specific drops or community moments (Fifth, Third, Alief) instead of a generic H-Town badge, and name the neighborhoods on the product story.

insights.title: Current stars with Houston on their backs
insights.detail: Travis Scott (Missouri City, Cactus Jack, Astroworld), Megan Thee Stallion (Texas Southern, Hot Girl branding) and Don Toliver repeatedly put Houston imagery in their work, and Rockets games are a regular celebrity-seat scene for the local rap class.
insights.implication: Player-artist content should be collaborative and local: Rockets players in the studios and shows of these artists. Jordan Brand ties to Cactus Jack mean any Travis crossover needs coordination across Nike and Jordan.

insights.title: Houston's older music is a design archive
insights.detail: Don Robey's Duke-Peacock label and Bronze Peacock club, Lightnin' Hopkins's Third Ward blues, Frenchtown zydeco (Clifton Chenier) and Tejano all created record sleeves, club posters and typography that predate rap and are rarely used in sportswear.
insights.implication: A vintage-label, record-sleeve story gives the City Edition a deeper source than the usual space and rocket imagery.

insights.title: Radio and the arena
insights.detail: 97.9 The Box (KBXX), KTSU 90.9 at Texas Southern and KPFT 90.1 carry the city's sound, and local anthems and slowed remixes are expected in Toyota Center production.
insights.implication: Seed products and capsules through Houston radio and DJs (screw-style mixes) as well as player channels.

places.name: Toyota Center
places.why: Rockets home and the stage for the touring rap, R&B and Latin acts that fill the city.

places.name: NRG Stadium and NRG Park
places.why: Home of the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo concert series and the former Astroworld Festival site.

places.name: Warehouse Live
places.why: Long-running mid-size room for hip-hop, rock and local showcases.

places.name: White Oak Music Hall
places.why: Multi-stage indoor-outdoor venue that books rap, indie and Latin acts.

places.name: Cactus Music
places.why: Long-standing independent record store with in-store performances.

places.name: Emancipation Park
places.why: Historic Black community park; Juneteenth gatherings and local music happen here.

places.name: KTSU 90.9 FM
places.why: Campus station that has long supported local hip-hop and jazz.

places.name: The Orange Show Center for Visionary Art
places.why: Organizer of the Art Car Parade and keeper of Houston's outsider-art, car-as-canvas tradition.

people.name: DJ Screw (Robert Earl Davis Jr., d. 2000)
people.role: DJ and originator of chopped and screwed
people.why: Founder of the sound and the Screwed Up Click; legacy is honored annually around his November anniversary.

people.name: Bun B and Paul Wall
people.why: Bun B of UGK (also runs Trill Burgers) and Paul Wall (grills, Swishahouse) are the most visible elders and regularly show up for Houston teams.

people.name: Scarface and the Geto Boys / Rap-A-Lot Records
people.role: Fifth Ward rap pioneers and label
people.why: Built Houston's first national rap identity; J. Prince's Rap-A-Lot is still active.

people.name: Travis Scott
people.why: Missouri City native and the biggest current Houston name; Astroworld is a city symbol, with the 2021 festival tragedy a sensitive history.

people.name: Megan Thee Stallion
people.why: Houston native, Texas Southern alum and frequent presence at the city's sporting events.

people.name: Beyonce
people.why: Grew up in Houston's Third Ward and keeps close ties to Houston, including Texas Southern and local charities.

people.name: Trae tha Truth
people.why: South Side figure known for Relief Gang and community aid, a model for authentic activation.

people.name: Maxo Kream and Tobe Nwigwe
people.why: Represent the diverse Southwest and immigrant-family Houston that the generic slab image misses.

moments.name: Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo concert series
moments.why: Largest annual music moment in the city, with country, Tejano, hip-hop and Latin nights at NRG Stadium; overlaps the Rockets' stretch run.

moments.name: Juneteenth in Third Ward and Fifth Ward
moments.why: Community gatherings and music in historic Black Houston neighborhoods; Texas has a particular claim to the holiday.

moments.name: DJ Screw anniversary tributes
moments.why: Mixes, listening events and community tributes mark his passing in November 2000; a respectful hook during Cup group play.

moments.name: Houston Art Car Parade
moments.why: Car-as-canvas culture that overlaps with slab imagery, around the playoff window.

moments.name: Rockets home games at Toyota Center
moments.timing: Every home game, Oct to April
moments.why: Arena DJ, halftime and local-artist moments; rapper and R&B celebrity attendance.

vocabulary.meaning: A customized car (Slow, Loud and Bangin'), usually a candy-painted older American sedan with chrome wheels and a loud sound system.
Wheels that stick out from the car's body, the most visible slab modification.
Slowed, pitched-down remixes with turntable cuts, created by DJ Screw.
DJ Screw's crew, including Lil' Keke, Big Moe, Fat Pat and Z-Ro.
Local shorthand for Houston and its original area code.
Nickname tied to the Rockets' 1994-95 title teams; used by fans and in apparel.
Custom gold or diamond teeth, a Houston staple associated with Paul Wall.
Bun B and UGK's blend of true and real, a Houston badge of authenticity.

designCues.cue: Candy apple red, the slab paint finish
designCues.source: Slab paint culture; also near the Rockets red
designCues.use: Deep, glossy red-to-black fades on uppers and jersey panels, with metallic flake finishes.

designCues.source: Slab candy paint and Screw-era tape art
designCues.use: Accent gradients and midsole colors; avoid any drug reference in naming.
Mirror-chrome swoosh and hardware with a mirror finish, referencing wheel spokes in outsoles.

designCues.source: The Rockets' retro red and yellow, per Secret Houston reporting
designCues.use: Pair gold-yellow with candy red for a music-flavored throwback colorway.

designCues.source: Screw tapes and local mixtape covers
designCues.use: Hand-lettered, stretched and slanted display type for hits and graphic tees; credit the original artists.
Illustrated trunk-scene graphics for tees and hoodies, commissioned from Houston artists.
Peacock-feather and record-label motifs for a heritage capsule; check rights first.
Metallic gold foils and tooth-like embossing as small detail.

productHooks: A Slab capsule: candy-red and chrome footwear and a satin bomber with trunk-display graphics, designed with Houston slab builders and artists.
A Screwed capsule: slowed-gradient apparel and mixtape-style packaging with a Rockets playlist produced with Houston DJs, timed to November.
A Third Ward and Fifth Ward neighborhood series with named local artists, where a share of proceeds goes to community groups.
A City Edition or throwback tie-in using the ketchup-and-mustard palette with record-label graphics.
watchouts: Do not use drug references (purple drank, lean) in names or graphics; the culture has been shaped by real loss.
DJ Screw's name, tape art, and Rap-A-Lot, Swishahouse and Cactus Jack graphics are third-party IP requiring licenses and estate or label approval.
Astroworld carries the 2021 festival tragedy; avoid Astroworld branding unless Travis Scott's team leads.
Slab culture belongs to Black Houston; pay and credit builders and clubs, and do not use it as costume.
